 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Anticipatory Bail Application (Stamp) No.
 1825 Of 2020
 Allabaksha Moulana Shaikh .. Applicant
 V/s.
 The State of Maharashtra ..Respondent
 ----
 Mr. Sachin Deokar for the Applicant.
 Mr. Y. M. Nakhwa, App for the Respondent-State.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Date : 12th October, 2020 (Through Video Conference) P.C. . Heard the learned counsels for the
parties.
2.  By a reasoned order dated 14/9/2020, the applicant was granted interim anticipatory bail.

Today,
during the course of hearing, it transpires that except the offence under Section 328 of IPC, other offences namely under Section 188, 272 and 273 of IPC are bailable.

Even the offence under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ('the said Act' for short) which carries a maximum punishment of imprisonment of six months, going by Part II of Schedule annexed Cr.P.C., would be a bailable offence.
It is not pointed out from any of the provisions contained in the said Act, Mamta Kale page 1 of 2 22 ABA st 1825-20 that the offence under Section 59 has been made non bailable.

Coming to Section 328 of the IPC, prima facie, there are no allegations that the applicant had administered any such stupefying or unwholesome drug or any other thing with intent to cause hurt to any person.

Prima facie, it appears that the only allegation is about the transport of the material which was prohibited in view of the order dated 15/7/2019 passed by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Maharashtra State, which is an offence under Section 59 of the said Act.
